pumac-2025-combinatorics-a-07.title: Recurrences for the ladder
pumac-2025-combinatorics-a-07.body:
The graph is a ladder with $2025$ rungs: $2025$ pairs of vertices $(A_n,B_n)$ joined by a rung, consecutive pairs joined by two rails ($2025+2\cdot2024=6073$ edges). Process the rungs from the right end. Let $C(n)$ be the expected number of components of the part from rung $n$ onwards (counting from the right, $n$ rungs), and let $D(n)$ be the same expectation when $A_n$ and $B_n$ are additionally joined by an undeletable extra connection (representing a path through the left part).

Add a new rung with its two rails and rung edge: three edges, each kept independently with probability $\frac12$.

*$C(n)$:* no edge deleted (prob $\frac18$): the new rung is joined to the old part and $A$, $B$ are connected through it, giving $D(n-1)$; exactly one edge deleted (prob $\frac38$): no new component, the pair is still attached somewhere, contributing $C(n-1)$; two deleted (prob $\frac38$): one new component, $1+C(n-1)$; all three deleted ($\frac18$): $2+C(n-1)$. So
$$C(n)=\tfrac18D(n-1)+\tfrac78C(n-1)+\tfrac58 .$$
*$D(n)$:* now $A_n$ and $B_n$ are always connected (the extra connection), so the rung is irrelevant and only the two rails matter. Both rails kept (prob $\frac14$): $A_{n-1},B_{n-1}$ become connected through the new pair, giving $D(n-1)$; exactly one rail kept ($\frac12$): $C(n-1)$; no rail kept ($\frac14$): the new pair is a separate component, $1+C(n-1)$. So
$$D(n)=\tfrac14D(n-1)+\tfrac34C(n-1)+\tfrac14 .$$
With $C(1)=\frac32$, $D(1)=1$. Put $E=C-D$: $E(n)=\frac18E(n-1)+\frac38$, $E(1)=\frac12$, so $E(n)=\frac37+\frac1{14}\big(\frac18\big)^{n-1}$. Then $C(n)=C(n-1)+\frac47-\frac1{14}\big(\frac18\big)^{n-1}$, so
$$C(n)=\frac32+\frac47(n-1)-\frac1{98}\Big(1-8^{-(n-1)}\Big).$$
(Checks: $C(2)=\frac{33}{16}$, $C(3)=\frac{337}{128}$, which agree with a direct enumeration of the small ladders.)

For $n=2025$: $49C=\frac{147}{2}+28\cdot2024-\frac12+\varepsilon=73.5+56672-0.5+\varepsilon=56745+\varepsilon$ with $\varepsilon=\frac12 8^{-2024}$ negligible. The nearest integer is $56745$.

**Answer: 56745**

pumac-2025-combinatorics-a-08.title: Shoelace formula and pair sums
pumac-2025-combinatorics-a-08.body:
The weighted area $A=\int w\,dA$ of a closed polygon is given by the shoelace formula $A=\frac12\sum_k\det(S_k,S_{k+1})$, where $S_k$ are the successive positions. If the steps in order are $w_1,\dots,w_8$ then $S_k=w_1+\dots+w_k$ and
$$A=\tfrac12\sum_{r<s}\det(w_r,w_s).$$
Label the eight step vectors $v_1,\dots,v_8$ and put $c_{ij}=\det(v_i,v_j)$ (so $c_{ji}=-c_{ij}$). Let $\sigma_{ij}=+1$ if $v_i$ comes before $v_j$ and $-1$ otherwise. Then $A=\frac12\sum_{i<j}c_{ij}\sigma_{ij}$ and
$$E[A^2]=\tfrac14\sum_{i<j}\sum_{k<l}c_{ij}c_{kl}\,E[\sigma_{ij}\sigma_{kl}].$$
- If $\{i,j\}\cap\{k,l\}=\emptyset$ the two signs are independent with mean $0$: contribution $0$.
- If $(i,j)=(k,l)$: $E=1$, contribution $S_2=\sum_{i<j}c_{ij}^2$.
- If the pairs share exactly one index, say the three indices are $a<b<c$: $E[\sigma_{ab}\sigma_{ac}]=\frac13$, $E[\sigma_{ab}\sigma_{bc}]=-\frac13$, $E[\sigma_{ac}\sigma_{bc}]=\frac13$ (e.g. $\sigma_{ab}\sigma_{ac}=1$ iff $a$ is first or last among the three, probability $\frac23$). Counting both orders of the two pairs gives the contribution $\frac23S_3$ with
$$S_3=\sum_{a<b<c}\big(c_{ab}c_{ac}-c_{ab}c_{bc}+c_{ac}c_{bc}\big).$$
Thus $E[A^2]=\frac14\big(S_2+\frac23S_3\big)$.

**Evaluating $S_3$.** Since $\sum_m v_m=0$, for each $j$: $0=\det(v_j,\sum_mv_m)=\sum_{m>j}c_{jm}-\sum_{m<j}c_{mj}$. So with $L_j=\sum_{i<j}c_{ij}$ we also have $\sum_{k>j}c_{jk}=L_j$. Then
$$\sum_{a<b<c}c_{ab}c_{ac}=\tfrac12\sum_a\Big(L_a^2-\sum_{t>a}c_{at}^2\Big),\quad \sum_{a<b<c}c_{ab}c_{bc}=\sum_bL_b^2,\quad \sum_{a<b<c}c_{ac}c_{bc}=\tfrac12\sum_c\Big(L_c^2-\sum_{t<c}c_{tc}^2\Big),$$
and therefore $S_3=-\tfrac12S_2-\tfrac12S_2=-S_2$. Hence $E[A^2]=\frac14\big(S_2-\frac23S_2\big)=\frac{S_2}{12}$.

**Computing $S_2=\sum_{i<j}\det(v_i,v_j)^2$.** Axis vectors $(\pm1,0),(0,\pm1)$: the $4$ orthogonal pairs give $1$ each: $4$. Diagonal vectors $(\pm1,\pm1)$: the $4$ perpendicular pairs have $|\det|=2$, giving $4$ each: $16$. Axis-diagonal pairs: all $16$ have $|\det|=1$: $16$. So $S_2=36$ and
$$E[A^2]=\frac{36}{12}=3.$$
(A direct average over all $8!$ orders confirms this.)

**Answer: 3**
